input.prompt:
TOOL ENVIRONMENT

All tools are served offline by `corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py` (path relative to the task-set
root). The server is deterministic: the same call always returns the same bytes. There is no
network.

Two equivalent ways to reach it:

  * MCP, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio:   `python3 corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py mcp`
    supporting `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`;
  * direct:                         `python3 corpora/mcp_toolset/server.py call <tool> '<json>'`

The full schema of all 84 tools is in `corpora/mcp_toolset/tools.json`. Three catalogue tools -
`catalog.list_tools`, `catalog.describe_tool` and `catalog.search_tools` - let you inspect the
toolset without committing to a data tool.

TOOL DISCIPLINE (read this before your first data call)

Every tool declares a `family`. Within a family the tools look interchangeable and are not:
one returns the value that answers a question of that kind, and its siblings return something
adjacent - a template rather than the resolved value, a cached copy that is no longer valid,
a published default rather than the binding one, a raw figure rather than the adjusted one.
Each tool's description says which it is.

You are scored on tool selection as well as on the answer. Calling a sibling of the tool you
needed - even once, even only to look - counts against you. Calling the three `catalog.*` tools
never counts against you: use them to decide.

DATA ACCESS RULE

The directory `corpora/mcp_toolset/fixtures/` holds the server's backing data. It is out of bounds: do not open, read, grep or otherwise inspect any file under it, and do not read `server.py` for the purpose of recovering values from it. Every value in your answer must come back to you through a tool call.

TASK

An incident opened against the service `kestrel-billing` at 2032-03-14T02:40:00Z. The incident
review needs to record who was actually carrying the primary pager at that instant - not who
the published rotation had pencilled in - and who that person is.

Report their full legal name as the directory holds it today, the team they are in today, and
the escalation tier they held for that service at that instant.

Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose before or after it, no markdown
code fence.

{
  "engineer_full_name": "<string>",
  "team": "<string>",
  "escalation_tier": <integer>
}

expected_behavior: The run inspects the toolset, selects the tool that resolves the rotation after approved overrides rather than the tool that returns the published template, takes the handle it returns, resolves that handle to a single current person record rather than running a fuzzy name search or reading a stale synced snapshot, and emits the three fields. The audit log shows no call into a contested family other than the two required tools.
quality_metric:
Two components, both reported.
(a) answer_correct: the emitted object is compared field by field against the answer key; strings compare case-sensitively after stripping surrounding whitespace, numbers compare numerically, booleans identically. answer_correct = true iff all 3 fields match.
(b) tool_selection: the run's tool-call record (the JSONL written by the server when `LAB001_TOOL_AUDIT` is set) is read. `contested_families` for this task are ["oncall-resolution", "person-resolution"]. A WRONG-TOOL INVOCATION is any recorded call to a tool whose declared `family` is in contested_families and which is not in the required tool set named by the answer key. Calls to tools in the `meta` family are never wrong-tool invocations. Calls to tools in families outside contested_families are recorded as extraneous calls and do not affect the score.
quality_score = 1.0 if answer_correct and wrong_tool_invocations == 0; 0.0 otherwise. task_success = (quality_score == 1.0).
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) one or more wrong-tool invocations, as defined in quality_metric over contested_families ["oncall-resolution", "person-resolution"] - this is the frozen workload-D zero-tolerance criterion (methodology v1.0.0 section 6); (2) any answer field does not match the answer key; (3) the reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with exactly the required keys; (4) the run answers without calling any tool; (5) the run edits `corpora/mcp_toolset/`; (6) the run reads any file under `corpora/mcp_toolset/fixtures/`, which makes the tool-selection measurement meaningless.
notes: Three separate wrong answers are reachable: the template holder rather than the override holder, a former employee with a near-identical name from the fuzzy search, and a stale team name from the directory-sync snapshot.
